svg.title: PGD-3 as a subset of FGSM, and the held-out matched contrasts
svg.desc: Panel A: schematic with illustrative values for six RGB-channel coordinates in the case where all three PGD steps have nonzero gradient. In that case, after 8-bit rounding, PGD-3 keeps FGSM's sign on the coordinates where all three step signs agree and is zero elsewhere. Steps with zero gradient can instead produce rounding ties; the text documents 0 to 7 such coordinates per image. Panel B: held-out contrasts in margin drop for 48 scene groups, one dot per group. PGD-3 subset minus random subset: mean +6.50, 95% interval +6.08 to +6.92. Top-gradient-magnitude subset minus random subset: mean -1.38, 95% interval -1.71 to -1.06.
svg.text: 8-bit rounding turns PGD-3 into a subset of FGSM
Schematic: six RGB-channel coordinates, illustrative values, all steps nonzero
Case shown: every step's gradient is nonzero and values stay inside [0, 1]. Then steps of ε/4
never reach the ε-ball boundary, so each displacement is ±¼ε or ±¾ε, and rounding to the 8-bit
grid (spacing ε) sends ±¼ε to 0 and ±¾ε to ±ε. A coordinate survives only if all three step
signs agree, and it then carries FGSM's sign (shaded). A zero-gradient step can leave ±½ε,
a rounding tie (observed: 0–7 coordinates per image; §3). The compared masks (PGD-3, random,
top-|∇|) each keep k of FGSM's coordinates at one level with FGSM's sign there; only the choice
of coordinates differs, so counts of + and − can differ between masks.
48 independent scene groups; difference in margin drop, logits
Margin-drop difference (logits); right = more damage than random
Dots: one per scene group, averaged over the two source contexts; random = mean of 8 seeds.
Bar: mean and 95% percentile bootstrap CI over groups (9,999 draws), from the frozen analysis.
Within each source context, PGD-3's subset beat all 8 random subsets in 48 of 48 groups.
